newsitem.title: CHINA: FORECAST - Shanghai state debt trade to cool down.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Shanghai state debt trade to cool down.

text.p: Trading on the Shanghai state debt repurchase and spot markets is expected to gradually cool down, mainly because of the establishment of a national debt depository, analysts said on Sunday.

The depository would gradually cut the extent to which institutions can trade state debt on different exchanges and trading centres using the same certificates, resulting in slower trading on the Shanghai market, they said.
The Shanghai market accounts for more than 95 percent of the spot treasury debt traded across China. Futures trading on state debt is banned.
Prices were also expected to move in a narrower range over the next few weeks as the impact of the new depository was felt, the analysts said.

Beijing announced on April 18 that it had set up the China Government Securities Depository Trust and Clearing Co, which will be responsible for holding, clearing and settling all state debt transactions.
All investors and institutions are required to deposit their treasury debt certificates at the new depository, and regional markets must transfer certificates deposited locally to it.
No deadline has been set for the transfer.
"With state debt certificates gradually being transferred to the national depository, trading on the Shanghai markets will gradually cool down," said one state debt trader.

"But the spot contracts are supported by their high yields (compared to the yields on new state debt issues) and the repo rates by a bull run on the (domestic) A share markets. So prices will not fall sharply," he added.
One of the aims of the new depository is to end the practice by which market players use one certificate to make multiple trades simultaneously.

"Institutions will no longer be able to trade on different exchanges and trading centres using the same state debt certificates," said a state debt investment analyst. "This will reduce volumes on the Shanghai market."

Daily volume of the Shanghai spot market, currently averaging around 1.5 million lots, could fall to around one million while volume on the repurchase market, now around eight million a day, could drop to five or six million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan ($121) face value of treasury debt.

Analysts said a short-lived burst of activity is expected on the spot market in late May when the first year installment coupon payments on the market barometer 10-year treasury bond, which matures in June 2006, fall due.
The bond, which closed at 119.12 yuan on Friday, could be pushed up to around 123 yuan before the payment in mid-June, analysts said.
The bond bears an annual coupon rate of 11.83 percent paid on annual basis instead of on maturity as with most other Chinese state debt.

The annual coupon of 9.18 percent for the new issue of 40 billion yuan in three-year treasury notes in May was significantly lower than the average yields for the spot contracts, which would help keep prices from falling, they said.
The continuing bull run on the domestic A share markets in Shanghai and Shenzhen was also expected to continue to help keep the state debt repurchase market active, they said.
Fund demand on the repo market now comes nearly exclusively from the stock markets, which have been on an upward trend since the beginning of the year.
Turnover on the repurchase market was expected to remain solid despite a fall in the past two weeks after Beijing announced the set-up of the new depository, analysts said. ($1 = 8.3 Chinese yuan)
